newsitem.title: CHINA: KFC sees more than 500 outlets in China by 2000.
newsitem.headline: KFC sees more than 500 outlets in China by 2000.

text.p: Kentucky Fried Chicken expects to have 500 outlets in China by 2000, up from the current 112, Eric Han, general manager of Shanghai KFC, said.

Nationwide sales in China in the first half of 1996 were 1.0 billion yuan, of which 250 million were from their 24 outlets in Shanghai, double the turnover in the city in the same 1995 period, he said in an interview on Friday.
Asia is the fastest growing market for KFC in the world, with China the fastest growth market in Asia, Han said.
Shanghai KFC is 49 percent owned by Shanghai New Asia and Pepsico Restaurants International.
KFC has become the world's biggest fried chicken fast food chain with about 10,000 restaurants in over 70 countries, a company statement said.
